content.title: Steam Community :: Guide :: Thaumaturge 100% Achievement Guide
content.text:
Genius Be mindful - Fully develop the Mind dimension. For this, you'll want Lelek (Main Quest) & Morana (Side Quest) to fully develop the Mind dimension. Rhetorician Keep your word. Fully develop the Word dimension. This requires Veles (Main Quest) and Krampus (Side Quest) in order to fully level the Word dimension. Wings of Pride Be guided by Pride and let your Flaw mature. This achievement is intended for your Pride playthrough. As you use Pride related dialogue options, your flaw becomes stronger until it starts to make decisions for you. This is relatively easy to achieve, even if you don't use them all the time. On my Pride playthrough I got it near the end of Act 1. But it does effect certain endings. ... Thaumaturge Get all the achievements. What a long road, but we made it! I hope this guide can help some in their pursuit of 100% Please feel free to leave comments below with corrections or your own strategies, as I'm always looking to make my guides better.

Trill-seeker Catch Lelek prowling the streets of southern Srodmiesce. ~Unlocks after your fight with Lelek. A Snake in Hand... Catch Veles, the salutor lured into the Imperial Hotel. ~Unlocks after your fight with Veles. Chapter II. Stakes and Costs Learn about a particular court secret. ~Unlocks at the end of Act 1. Chapter III. This Is Getting Serious Leave the clinic and greet the martial law in Warsaw. ~Unlocks at the end of Act 2. My Work Here Is Done Get to the end of the adventure. ~Unlocks at the end of Act 3. ... Slippery Situation Catch Morana, the salutor of Powisle. Upon reaching Powisle, find your way to the docks where "The Art Of Dying" side quest begins. Here you are tasked with catching a killer. (Must be completed before Act 2.) Afterward, a new quest "Horses In The Sky" will follow that requires Word Dimension 5 to continue. Once you solve the murders, you'll have to wait for a phone call.

Genius Be mindful - Fully develop the Mind dimension. For this, you'll want Lelek (Main Quest) & Morana (Side Quest) to fully develop the Mind dimension. Rhetorician Keep your word. Fully develop the Word dimension. This requires Veles (Main Quest) and Krampus (Side Quest) in order to fully level the Word dimension. Wings of Pride Be guided by Pride and let your Flaw mature. This achievement is intended for your Pride playthrough. As you use Pride related dialogue options, your flaw becomes stronger until it starts to make decisions for you. This is relatively easy to achieve, even if you don't use them all the time. On my Pride playthrough I got it near the end of Act 1. But it does effect certain endings. ... Thaumaturge Get all the achievements. What a long road, but we made it! I hope this guide can help some in their pursuit of 100% Please feel free to leave comments below with corrections or your own strategies, as I'm always looking to make my guides better.

Complete Domination Win a fight with full Health Points. Easier than it sounds, due to Veles and Upyr's ability to heal us. The key to making this easy is learning to interrupt or postpone the enemy so they don't land a hit! Best attempted on an easy fight with few enemies. ... Hands Off Keep enemies from launching an attack during a fight. This is tough because it requires a proper strategy and the right fight. Find an early game encounter that has two enemies with low focus, and augment your focus attacks so that it does double when an enemy is suffering. Use Morana's interrupt to keep one of them eternally trapped, while you start breaking the focus of the other. Augment your quick punch with a 50% chance to interrupt and use Veles if you're in a tight spot. With luck, you'll get it! Peaceful Solution Win a fight only by imposing states on enemies.

Not So Fast Delay or interrupt the actions of 50 enemies. Should unlock naturally as you play the game! Breaking focus interrupts enemies, and you can augment attacks with interruption charms. Morana also has an interrupt ability that can be pretty strong. Fast and Nervous Win a skirmish in 6 rounds or less. This should unlock rather quickly, a lot fights only have 2 enemies, especially in the early game. Factory of Pain Inflict 1,001 damage to your enemies. It sounds like a scary number, but some attacks do 40+ on their own so the damage numbers rack up pretty quickly! ... Eternal Suffering Impose the state of Suffering 100 time on your enemies. I really liked Bukavac, because he can set up a lot of things with Suffering. His final attack is very strong at spreading Suffering. Along with this, you yourself can spread suffering and augment your skills to generate more of it.

content.title: The Thaumaturge: List of all Salutors, map - gamepressure.com
content.text:
How to unlock: You may miss this Salutor. You have to complete 2 side quests in the Powisle district - The Art of Dying and Horses in the sky. Only then can Wiktor meet the person with Flaw and fight Morana boss. Recommended skills: Morana's two basic attacks can drain focus. In our opinion, Pestilent Breath is better because it can interrupt the opponent's planned attack. The Price of Peace works well on enemies with severely depleted focus. ... How to unlock: You may miss this Salutor. You must start the side quest A rod for the hero in Port Praga district. Wiktor will catch up with the character with Flaw, triggering a fight with the Krampus boss. Recommended skills: In addition to depleting the enemy's focus, Fiendish Prank can also regenerate Wiktor's focus at the cost of small amounts of health points. Deadly Schnapps is a slow attack that is best used only after various enemies have lost some focus.

Upyr, Bukavac, Weles, Lelek, Morana, Genie, Golem and Krampus are unique Salutors from the game The Thaumaturge. This guide page explains how to recruit each creature and the best skills of the available Salutors. ... In our The Thaumaturge guide you will find descriptions of all Salutors that Wiktor can tame - these are Upyr, Bukavac, Veles, Lelek, Morana, Djinn, Golem and Krampus. You will learn how to obtain individual creatures, what Dimensions they represent, and which Salutor skills are best to use. ... How to unlock: Not applicable - Upyr has been traveling with Wiktor from the very beginning of the game. Recommended skills: Liberum Veto is a good quick skill to deprive the opponent of a trait. content.text:
Flaws are a game mechanic in the video game, The Thaumaturge. Salutors are attracted to Flaws, and thaumaturges can pact bind salutors to themselves using these Flaws. ... Flaws are marks on the human soul, they can be caused by either by something traumatic or a constant routine. They are formed in the subconscious and centre around the things that matter most to someone. Flaws are sorted into four categories, called Dimensions, depending on what aspect of human experience they influence. There's the Heart, Mind, Deed, and Word Dimension. The Heart Dimension involves emotions. The Word Dimension involves things spoken. The Mind Dimension involves what is thought or contained within memories. The Deed Dimension involves actions and physicality. If the name is in italics that means it is a thaumaturge who acquired the Flaw, and not the original bearer.

content.title: The Thaumaturge - All Salutor Locations - BAI GAMING
content.text:
There are options not to take the Salutor but choose to take it (Grab the Flaw and face off against the Djinn) to recruit him. Do the “All Our Curses” main quest. There are three options right before the Golem boss fight that impact whether you recruit him, as well as the story in the game. “Say yes” means you let Ariel take Golem and Ariel will live and Ligia loses her Flaw. You won’t get the Golem if you choose this! “Fool Ariel” means you take Golem, Ariel will die, and Ligia keeps her Flaw. “Transfer Ligia’s Flaw” means you take Golem, Ariel will die, and Ligia loses her Flaw. Ariel is NOT required to live to get the best Coterie Route ending, you just lose out on some dialogue and he won’t help you with a forced enemy encounter (that’s easy enough to do on your own). Ligia’s Flaw only affects a small portion of the epilogue (I’d keep her flaw for a slightly better end but it doesn’t matter, you might get a Dimension bonus if you take the flaw so it’s up to you).

Salutors are esoteric supernatural creatures that players can recruit in The Thaumaturge. They can be used in battles to disable enemy Traits and come with a variety of their own abilities. Each Salutor is associated with one of four Dimensions – Word, Heart, Deed, and Mind, which influence responses in combat or exploration. By recruiting more Salutors, more portions of the skill trees will unlock, allowing you to upgrade combat abilities, being able to examine more objects when exploring, and Wiktor’s upgraded Dimensions can be used when talking to NPCs (Dimension speech checks will unlock). We’ll try not to spoil, but I will need to mention mission names and Salutor names and sometimes a small amount of plot associated with it (Golem is the only Salutor that has slight spoilers). We’ll generally go in the order you recruit Salutors in. There are 8 Salutors in total.

There are options not to take the Salutor but choose to take it (Grab the Flaw and face off against the Djinn) to recruit him. Do the “All Our Curses” main quest. There are three options right before the Golem boss fight that impact whether you recruit him, as well as the story in the game. “Say yes” means you let Ariel take Golem and Ariel will live and Ligia loses her Flaw. You won’t get the Golem if you choose this! “Fool Ariel” means you take Golem, Ariel will die, and Ligia keeps her Flaw. “Transfer Ligia’s Flaw” means you take Golem, Ariel will die, and Ligia loses her Flaw. Ariel is NOT required to live to get the best Coterie Route ending, you just lose out on some dialogue and he won’t help you with a forced enemy encounter (that’s easy enough to do on your own). Ligia’s Flaw only affects a small portion of the epilogue (I’d keep her flaw for a slightly better end but it doesn’t matter, you might get a Dimension bonus if you take the flaw so it’s up to you).

(If you want to do the Flying University optional side quest, I found that keeping her flaw helped me progress the questline more easily.) Go to the Port Praga region as soon as it’s unlocked on the map! It’s very missable. If you take a tram to Port Praga examine the northern area to find Real Fireworks observation to unlock the sidequest. The location to find The Real Fireworks clue is shown below. Follow The Real Fireworks quest and press the right trigger to find where to unlock the other clues. It’ll lead you to a warehouse and a new quest A Rod For A Hero. In general you can pick any option and it’ll lead to a fight against Krampus. Win the fight to recruit him. The only issue with this salutor is that it’s highly missable.

Make sure to see Rasputin after recruiting a new Salutor because Wiktor will be weakened until you get cured. I’ll mark which Salutors are easily missable. Sometimes you need to progress the story to unlock more regions you can travel to. ... Complete the prologue mission “Shadow of Sins Past” (main story). Go to Powisle and go to the eastern part of the map to start a series of quests. It starts with The Art of Dying, then after that you get the side quest Horses in the Sky. You might need to do Dimension checks to gather evidence, so you can wait a little to progress this questline later if you find yourself unable to progress. But it’s missable eventually, so try to make sure this side quest is still active your menu. We recruited Veles first (see below) to do the Dimension checks on evidence to help complete the mission, so consider nudging the main story forward a bit.

content.text:
After finishing the Prologue, players will realize that his dream has come true now with the help of the infamous Rasputin. Though Salutors are an amazing addition to the team in the game, they are relatively hard to find since they are supposed to be rare creatures. In the guide we will present all 8 Salutors and tell you when and how to tame them to help the Thaumaturge Wiktor in his exploration of Warsaw. Fool’s Theory have created exactly 8 Salutors that players can find in the RPG, with two for each Dimension: Heart, Word, Mind, and Deed. Four of them will join Wiktor no matter what by progressing the main quest, one will also be part of the main quest but will require a tough choice to join, and the other three are optional and easily missed. The 4 monsters that join you no matter what are each assigned to one of the 4 Dimensions, making sure that Wiktor also gets the +1 bonus in all of them for their respective Flaws.

Though Salutors are an amazing addition to the team in the game, they are relatively hard to find since they are supposed to be rare creatures. In the guide we will present all 8 Salutors and tell you when and how to tame them to help the Thaumaturge Wiktor in his exploration of Warsaw. Fool’s Theory have created exactly 8 Salutors that players can find in the RPG, with two for each Dimension: Heart, Word, Mind, and Deed. Four of them will join Wiktor no matter what by progressing the main quest, one will also be part of the main quest but will require a tough choice to join, and the other three are optional and easily missed. The 4 monsters that join you no matter what are each assigned to one of the 4 Dimensions, making sure that Wiktor also gets the +1 bonus in all of them for their respective Flaws.

Wiktor will get Upyr back in the first 30 minutes of playing The Thaumaturge, right after passing Rasputin’s test. This Salutor mainly works as a support companion, as he can heal the player, remove negative effects, and deal decent damage to enemies at full health. ... To get Bukavac, players will just need to complete the Prologue. Follow the main plot all the way into the woods and defeat the demon to get it to help you. Bukavac is a powerful DMG dealer that often inflicts Suffering on the enemies (this game’s bleed equivalent). Will generally finish your fights with her amazing anti-low health buffs. ... After pub-crawling with Abaurycy, you’ll stumble upon Danis, the one holding the key to Lelek’s companionship: his Flaw. Brace yourself for a game of Russian Roulette. Survive the gamble, and the Flaw will emerge, triggering a battle with Lelek himself.

Defeat this feathery foe, and he’ll join you as a powerful Mind Salutor. ... After a thorough investigation in Svetlana’s apartment, a strategic seance awaits. Navigate the session to draw out Sofya’s Flaw, triggering the summoning and subsequent battle with Veles. Win the Salutor fight, and this Word companion will join your ranks, no matter the previous choices. ... Getting Morana, the 2nd Mind Dimension Salutor, is a multi-stage process that unfolds across Act 1 and Act 2 of the game. While the initial investigation for the related murder case can be largely completed during Act 1 with a sufficient Word and Mind rating (Level 5) for Manipulation, successfully identifying the culprit does not directly grant access to Morana. Progression through Act 2 is necessary to complete the acquisition process. Following your initial conversation with Ligia in Act 2, you will receive a crucial phone call from Pelevin.

Completing a series of main quests, namely “All Our Curses,” “A Great Uproar,” and “Clay Ambitions,” will lead to a choice where the player will decide if they will take Golem as their Salutor or not. Similar to Djinn, Golem presents a unique choice. You have the option to: Retain Golem within your party. Bestow Golem upon the Jewish Thaumaturge, Ariel Rofe. Ultimately, the decision rests with you, but the decision will have dire consequences when it comes to Ariel. And that is all you need to know about how to get all Salutors in The Thaumaturge. content.title: The Thaumaturge - The Devil's Gambit Walkthrough - Neoseeker
content.text:
We are about to go to a "place of no return" so we need to make sure everything is done. For starters, if you didn't do the sidequest we got in the previous main quest (Front Page), then go ahead and do that one. During that sidequest we (at least I) got 2 more sidequests. Both will be linked below. ... Now, a fairly important one to do! At this point we have 7 Salutors and we're missing 1! Let's go get it real quick. Travel over to Port Praga and once here approach the bulletin board near the carriage area (west-northwest of the barber) and read the note posted here called Fireworks advertisement. This will give us the LATEST FIREWORKS: "Golden Tiger" fireworks advertisement and start the quest to get the final Salutor (spoiler alert: he's the easiest fight). ... After that sidequest we immediately start another one. This is THE one where we actually get the salutor.

MAKE SURE TO SAVE YOUR GAME AND KEEP A COPY OF THIS SAVE FILE. THIS IS THE POINT IN THE GAME WHERE WE'LL ADVANCE TOWARDS THE "END GAME" AND WILL BE UNABLE TO PURSUE VARIOUS SIDE QUESTS AND URBAN SECRETS. YOU SHOULD REALLY ONLY CONTINUE THIS QUEST ONCE YOU'RE READY TO ENTER THE ENDGAME. With that said, head to Rasputin in his usual place and talk to him, confirming you are ready to head to the church to assist him. You'll see the game's warning before you go, but soon you'll get a lot of scenes as the two of you enter the church. Here, Rasputin will tell you of the exorcism that is about to be done, and asks for our help in, well, solving whatever the real problem is. You know, so he can take advantage of it as a "healer". So yeah, once you gain control in the church head north to find THE DEVIL'S DESIGNS: Book, then go north (past the kid) to find THE DEVIL'S DESIGNS: Holy Icon.

As you may have guessed by the whole "kid is seeing things" and "not lying about it", this kid is a Thaumaturge! Oh wow... Wiktor will do his thing here (talking directly to the kid in your mind space) and will calm him down, asking if he sees salutors. He does of course. Here, we will have to make a choice: do we want to TAKE the kid's flaw... or leave it be so he grows up like us. Since BK is going with Rasputin, he chose to take the Flaw. This helps Rasputin in what he's doing here after all. You can of course choose to leave the flaw if you want. This isn't the end-all be-all of choices. With that said, BK took the flaw of FRIGHT. We will get some scenes after this as Rasputin does his thing and proves himself in front of everyone. Well... with our help anyways. Going directly against the church too. That ought to get some attention. The quest will be complete shortly afterwards, but as you go to leave the church there are quite a few scenes.

These scenes lead into the next quest automatically, so go ahead and enjoy them and we'll see you in the next quest as always! ... Support our guide writers and staff so we can continue to make the best guides for all of your favourite games.

Welcome to our Guide and Walkthrough for The Thaumaturge (2024)! With this guide you can expect a full walkthrough of each of the game's chapters, strategies for all boss fights and much more! In this RPG, you will team up with ethereal beings called Salutors as our protagonist investigates various mysteries and supernatural events, makes morally ambiguous dialog choices, and overall just tries to make his way through 1900's Warsaw. This game is brought to us by developer Fool's Theory, and definitely has several things that ol' BK (and Vinheim) definitely enjoy. Turn-based RPG combat. Investigation mechanics. An isometric view. The very unique location... oh, and the fact that these Salutors absolutely look like metal versions of "personas" definitely fits in there too! ... Regardless, it's great to be on another adventure together everyone! You all know BK and Vin love our RPGs and mystery games, so let's jump into this unique eastern-european supernatural adventure together!

So the order has to be: complete every missable side quest including Djinn, Krampus, and Morana before you trigger the point of no return inside The Devil's Gambit. The Fright flaw from the child happens inside that same quest after you have already passed the point of no return, so you get it automatically if you choose to take it.

The practical reality for you right now: Djinn is in Mirów — Fearless side quest. If you have not done that yet it needs to happen before you go anywhere near The Devil's Gambit. Same for Krampus in Port Praga if you have not done Real Fireworks and A Rod for a Hero yet.

The ever-increasing complexity of synthetic gene networks and applications of synthetic biology requires precise and orthogonal gene expression systems. Of particular interest are systems responsive to light as they enable the control of gene expression dynamics with unprecedented resolution in space and time. While broadly used in mammalian backgrounds, however, optogenetic approaches in plant cells are still limited due to interference of the activating light with endogenous photoreceptors. Here, we describe the development of the first synthetic light-responsive system for the targeted control of gene expression in mammalian and plant cells that responds to the green range of the light spectrum in which plant photoreceptors have minimal activity. We first engineered a system based on the light-sensitive bacterial transcription factor CarH and its cognate DNA operator sequence CarO from Thermus thermophilus to control gene expression in mammalian cells.

content.title: Potent optogenetic regulation of gene expression in mammalian cells for bioproduction and basic research
content.text:
# Potent optogenetic regulation of gene expression in mammalian cells for bioproduction and basic research

**DOI:** 10.1093/nar/gkaf546

**Published:** 2025-06-30

**Authors:** Jeannette Gebel, Elisa Ciglieri, Rainer Stahl, Fraser Duthie, Fabian Frechen, Andreas Möglich, Herbert Müller-Hartmann, Hanns-Martin Schmidt, Dagmar Wachten



Compared to chemical inducers, light-dependent control of gene expression by optogenetics achieves a higher spatial and temporal resolution. Beyond basic research, this could also prove decisive for manufacturing difficult-to-express proteins in pharmaceutical bioproduction. However, current optogenetic gene-expression systems limit this application in mammalian cells, as expression levels and the degree of induction upon light stimulation are insufficient. To overcome this limitation, we designed a photoswitch by fusing the blue light-activated light–oxygen–voltage receptor EL222 from *Erythrobacter litoralis* to the three transcriptional activator domains VP64, p65, and Rta in tandem. The resultant photoswitch, dubbed DEL-VPR, allows up to a 570-fold induction of target gene expression by blue light, thereby achieving expression levels of strong constitutive promoters. 

The VP-EL222 was synthesized (Integrated DNA Technology) based on the sequence from Motta Mena *et al.* [[29]]. The VEL construct and VPR sequence were synthesized by GeneArt (Thermo Fisher). VP-EL222 and VEL were singularly cloned inside a pcDNA3.1 vector (Invitrogen) using *BamHI* and *XbaI* restriction sites. For the light-induced expression of firefly luciferase (fLuc), the constructs pGL4.23_5xC120-minP-FLuc and pcDNA3.1_5xC120-minP-FLuc were generously provided by Kevin Gardner. The plasmids encoding GAVTA and TAEL were generously provided by Stephanie Woo. The construct 5xC120-minP-mCherry, used for light-induced expression of the fluorescent reporter mCherry, was created by cloning polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-amplified mCherry into pcDNA3.1_5xC

Molecular switches that are controlled by chemicals have evolved as central research instruments in mammalian cell biology. However, these tools are limited in terms of their spatiotemporal resolution due to freely diffusing inducers. These limitations have recently been addressed by the development of optogenetic, genetically encoded, and light-responsive tools that can be controlled with the unprecedented spatiotemporal precision of light. In this article, we first provide a brief overview of currently available optogenetic tools that have been designed to control diverse cellular processes.
